# Bidirectional Markdown ⇄ Jira rich-text sync (Cloud ADF + DC wiki)

## Context / Problem
The Jira reconciler already routes ticket descriptions/comments through the
`RichTextCodec` seam (epic `e369`, story J3 / `aac8`), but the **current encode
is plain-text-structured, not Markdown-aware**: Cloud emits a plain-text ADF
(`adf.text_to_adf`, one paragraph per block) via `acli.py:205` / `acli_cli_ops.py:369`,
and DC's `WikiTextCodec` is an **identity** codec (plain string through). So the
Markdown structure authors write (headings, checklists, code, lists) shows up as
literal source in Jira, and rich text authored in Jira reads as noise in rebar.
We want each client to receive a native rich representation — **ADF** for Jira
Cloud, **wiki markup** for Jira Data Center — without a sync echo loop that would
ratchet Jira-specific formatting back into the store or erode content over
repeated passes. Validated over the real historical corpus (1,771 tickets /
5,568 bodies) by six de-risking experiments recorded in session log
`5eb0-52a3-45f0-43e5`.

## Approach
Two asymmetric codecs behind one state-based echo-safety layer, built ON the
existing `RichTextCodec` seam (`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`), because the
two Jira targets are fundamentally different formats:
- **Cloud = truly bidirectional, lossless.** Make the existing `AdfCodec` /
  `adf.py` encode **Markdown-aware** (it already emits ADF, just plain-text
  paragraphs today). `marklas` round-trips Markdown↔ADF at 99.64% fixed-point over
  the corpus — the structured-typed-node pattern, inherently echo-safe under
  normalize-both-sides.
- **DC = one-way MD→wiki render, bidirectional SYNC.** Replace `WikiTextCodec`'s
  identity outbound with a segmenting renderer. Jira wiki is a lossy text markup
  and no library round-trips rebar's punctuation-dense prose reliably (pandoc's
  jira reader misparses `->`, ASCII tables, and regex, and provably erodes them
  one char per pass). So DC renders one way over the units that are structurally
  safe, passes dangerous units through verbatim, and prevents loops with
  **state-based echo suppression** using the reconciler's existing per-binding
  baseline (ADR 0026, `binding_store.py:102`) — NOT codec fixed-point. Genuine
  human Jira edits are still detected against baseline and pulled back best-effort.

Echo-safety is state-based for both clients; concurrency is last-write-wins over a
three-way state (baseline/local/remote) so neither side's changes are ever
silently destroyed. State additions obey epic `0303`'s churn discipline
(change-gated, fixed-size, never a per-pass timestamp).

## Dependencies / sequencing
This epic must not be claimed until its three in-flight prerequisites close:
`0303` (tickets-store growth / committed-state format), `e369` (Jira-family DC
seam), `3e73` (Cloud↔DC test parity). These are recorded as `depends_on` links.

## Child responsibilities (decomposition)
- **Cloud ADF codec** — make the existing `AdfCodec`/`adf.py` encode
  Markdown-aware (vendor/pin `marklas`); Markdown↔ADF for descriptions and
  comments; fix the combined strong+strikethrough mark-order oscillator; accept
  the ~18 transient whitespace canonicalizations via normalize-both-sides; leave
  the shared plain-text `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text` unchanged. Delivers AC1.
- **DC one-way segmenting renderer** — implement `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`: split
  body into blocks/list-items, render structurally-safe units to wiki via pinned
  pandoc, substitute prose arrows on the Markdown BEFORE pandoc, verbatim-wrap
  ASCII tables in `{noformat}`, pass dangerous units through unchanged, reassemble,
  and wire `to_wire` into the DC outbound send. Delivers AC2.
- **DC robustness/perf hardening** — bound pandoc's per-field subprocess cost, add
  a hard timeout with plain-text fallback on pathological input, and satisfy
  pandoc GPL/SBOM compliance. Delivers AC2 under production constraints.
- **State echo suppression + LWW conflict safety** — reuse the ADR-0026 baseline
  (observed-after-push canonical form) and the codec's existing `normalize_outbound`
  compare op plus a change-gated inline `rich_sha`; three-way LWW that always flags
  concurrent conflict; origin-gated outbound so Jira-native constructs survive.
  Delivers AC3, AC4, AC5.
- **Comment sync (append-only)** — persistent Jira-comment-ID map (replacing
  body-equality identity); rebar→Jira creation and inbound new-comment mirroring
  only (no edit/delete sync), rendered through the same codec seam; descriptions
  cut over before comments. Delivers the comment portion of AC1/AC2.
- **Live DC harness + cross-repo contract** — extend the existing Docker Jira DC
  harness to assert rendered-HTML fidelity (not just wiki source), and add a
  contract test pinning `normalize_rich_text` back-compat for the sibling
  `agentic-dev-platform` importer. Delivers AC6.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cloud descriptions and comments sync as Markdown-aware ADF and round-trip
  Markdown↔ADF with no perpetual re-sync over the historical corpus; verified by a
  corpus idempotence test that asserts convergence (incl. the two known
  combined-mark bodies).
- [ ] DC descriptions and comments render to wiki for structurally-safe content
  while remaining echo-safe with zero content erosion over ≥5 repeated passes,
  including the known ASCII-table ratchet body; verified by a corpus echo-safety
  test asserting no monotonic length decay.
- [ ] A reconcile pass in which no body changed writes 0 new committed-state
  entries and no per-pass timestamp attributable to this feature; verified by the
  git-delta cost harness reproducing the ≤0.07 KB/version stable profile.
- [ ] A concurrent edit on both sides is always detected and flagged rather than
  silently overwritten; verified by the concurrent-conflict regression test over
  the corpus (the proven 799/799-detected invariant).
- [ ] A Jira-authored native construct (panel/mention/date) survives a subsequent
  rebar-originated reconcile pass; verified by an origin-gating test.
- [ ] The end-to-end behavior runs against a live Jira DC instance asserting
  rendered HTML (via `?expand=renderedFields`), not just wiki source; verified by
  the extended Docker DC harness CI job.
